questions.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of siblings of each of $22$ students.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Siblings }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&0\\ 1&7\\ 2&9\\ 3&4\\ 4&2\\ 5&0\end{array}$
What is the range?

options.why: Used $5 - 0$, counting the values whose frequency is $0$ even though no student has them.
Subtracted the smallest frequency from the largest frequency ($9 - 2$) instead of using the data values.
Reported the greatest frequency rather than the spread of the data values.

questions.solution_text:
$x = 0$ and $x = 5$ have frequency $0$, so no student has $0$ or $5$ siblings.
$\text{Range} = 4 - 1$
$= 3$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9]\draw[->] (-0.6,0)--(5.2,0);\foreach \x in {0,1,2,3,4} {\draw (\x,-0.08)--(\x,0.08); \node[below,font=\scriptsize] at (\x,-0.1) {$\x$};}\foreach \x/\c in {0/3,1/5,2/2,3/4,4/1} {\foreach \k in {1,...,\c} {\fill (\x,{0.3*\k}) circle (2pt);}}\node[font=\scriptsize] at (2,2.1) {Goals per match};\node[below,font=\scriptsize] at (2,-0.9) {Goals scored};\end{tikzpicture}

The dot plot shows the number of goals a team scored in each of $15$ matches. What is the mean number of goals per match, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Averaged the five different scores $0,1,2,3,4$ and ignored how often each one occurs.
Averaged the frequencies ($15 \div 5$) instead of averaging the data values.
Divided $\Sigma fx$ by the number of different scores ($25 \div 5$) instead of by $\Sigma f$.

questions.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of books each of $29$ students read last month.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Books }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&2\\ 1&3\\ 2&4\\ 3&5\\ 4&10\\ 5&5\end{array}$
What is the median?

options.why: Gave the median position $\frac{n+1}{2}$ instead of the score sitting at that position.
Reported the greatest frequency rather than the middle data value.
Reported the cumulative frequency at the median position instead of the data value there.

questions.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c}x&f&\text{c.f.}\\ \hline 0&2&2\\ 1&3&5\\ 2&4&9\\ 3&5&14\\ 4&10&24\\ 5&5&29\end{array}$
$\text{Position} = \frac{29 + 1}{2}$
$= 15$
The cumulative frequency first reaches $15$ at $x = 4$.
$\text{Median} = 4$

questions.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of pets in each household surveyed.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Pets }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&5\\ 1&9\\ 2&6\\ 3&3\\ 4&2\end{array}$
How many pets do the surveyed households have altogether?

options.why: Added the frequency column, which gives the number of households surveyed, not the number of pets.
Added the data-value column ($0+1+2+3+4$) without multiplying each value by its frequency.
Added the number of households to the number of pets ($25 + 38$), counting each household twice.
Gave $50\%$ of the total cumulative frequency instead of the score it reads across to.
Read the cumulative frequency where the ogive is met rather than the score below that point.
Read down to the score at the left of where the ogive crosses the halfway line, giving the value one below the median.

questions.solution_text:
$50\%$ of the total is $\frac{25}{2} = 12.5$.
Reading across from $12.5$ to the ogive and down lands in the $x = 2$ column.
$\text{Median} = 2$

options.why: Read the cumulative frequency at $x = 2$ without subtracting the cumulative frequency before it.
Subtracted the wrong pair, $10 - 4$, which gives the frequency of $1$ goal instead of $2$ goals.
Subtracted the next pair up, $23 - 19$, which gives the frequency of $3$ goals.

questions.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of pets in each of $24$ households.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Pets }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&3\\ 1&5\\ 2&4\\ 3&8\\ 4&4\end{array}$
What is the median?

options.why: Took the value whose cumulative frequency first passes $12.5$ without checking that the $12$th score is only $2$.
Used the $12$th score alone instead of averaging it with the $13$th score.
Reported the greatest frequency rather than the middle data value.

questions.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c}x&f&\text{c.f.}\\ \hline 0&3&3\\ 1&5&8\\ 2&4&12\\ 3&8&20\\ 4&4&24\end{array}$
$\text{Position} = \frac{24 + 1}{2}$
$= 12.5$
The cumulative frequency reaches exactly $12$ at $x = 2$, so the $12$th score is $2$ and the $13$th score is $3$.
$\text{Median} = \frac{2 + 3}{2}$
$= 2.5$

questions.question_text:
The frequency table shows the number of days each of $21$ students was absent last week.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Days absent }(x)&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0&8\\ 1&3\\ 2&0\\ 3&6\\ 4&4\end{array}$
Which set of summary statistics is correct?

options.why: Reported the greatest frequency $8$ as the mode instead of the data value $0$ it belongs to.
Treated the table as a plain list of rows: took the range from the frequency column ($8 - 0 = 8$) and the middle row of the $x$ column ($x = 2$) as the median, ignoring the frequencies.
Made both slips at once: read the mode as the largest frequency $8$, and used the row positions for the range ($8 - 0$) and the median ($x = 2$).

questions.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c|c}x&f&\text{c.f.}\\ \hline 0&8&8\\ 1&3&11\\ 2&0&11\\ 3&6&17\\ 4&4&21\end{array}$
$\text{Mode} = 0$
$\text{Range} = 4 - 0$
$= 4$
$\text{Position} = \frac{21 + 1}{2}$
$= 11$
The cumulative frequency first reaches $11$ at $x = 1$.
$\text{Median} = 1$
